Miser

MY-zer · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Miser is one who hoards wealth.

Everyone in town assumed the reclusive landlord was a miser, until his will revealed he had secretly been funding the local shelter for decades.

Worked Example

The story's miser kept every dollar he ever earned hidden under his floorboards, wearing the same threadbare coat winter after winter rather than spend a single coin.

A person who obsessively hoards money and refuses to spend it, even when they clearly could, is exactly what a miser is.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

skinflint: A skinflint is stingy in everyday dealings — dodging the bill, tipping nothing, haggling over pennies with the waiter. A miser goes further than cheapness toward others: he hoards wealth itself, piling money up and guarding the pile as the whole point of his life.

tightwad: A tightwad simply hates parting with money, even for small comforts of his own. A miser adds the hoard: he does not just avoid spending — he piles wealth up and clings to it, finding his satisfaction in the growing pile itself.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

spendthrift: a person who spends money wastefully

philanthropist: a person who gives generously to good causes

Where it sits · how fiercely they cling to money — saver → miser → hoarder

saver vs. miser: Saver is far milder than miser: a saver sets money aside sensibly, while a miser clings to wealth with a much fiercer, joyless grip.

hoarder vs. miser: Hoarder is more extreme than miser: a miser hoards money and hates spending it, but a hoarder goes further, compulsively piling up possessions of every kind and refusing to let anything go.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — miser (miser)

root — miser (miser): wretched, unhappy (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Miser comes directly from the Latin word miser, 'wretched' or 'unhappy' -- the same root behind misery and miserable. Older writers saw hoarding wealth as a kind of self-inflicted misery, refusing life's comforts for the sake of money.

Use the root in a new word: miserable

Use the root in a new word: miserable: Stuck in traffic for three hours in the summer heat, the whole family arrived at the reunion feeling absolutely miserable.

Root Check

Word Choice

Miser names the person, not just the behavior -- it's the specific kind of hoarding, joyless person that avarice (earlier in this unit) can produce. Not every greedy person is technically a miser, but every miser is driven by avarice.
